results.title: Generators of Gardam's presentation
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: This is the two-element set consisting of the distinct formal symbols $a$ and $b$, which serve as the generators of the group presentation in Theorem A of Gardam's counterexample to the unit conjecture.

results.title: First free generator of Gardam's presentation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: $a$ is the generator $a$, viewed as an element of the free group on the two generators $a$ and $b$.

results.title: Second free generator of Gardam's presentation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: $b$ is the generator $b$, viewed as an element of the free group on the two generators $a$ and $b$.

results.title: Relators of Gardam's group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the free group on the generators $a$ and $b$, the relators are the two elements $b^{-1}a^2ba^2$ and $a^{-1}b^2ab^2$.

results.title: Gardam's group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: $P$ is the group with generators $a$ and $b$ and relators $b^{-1}a^2ba^2$ and $a^{-1}b^2ab^2$, that is, $P = \langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2}, a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$.

results.title: The element x of Gardam's group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group $P$ with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2},\ a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$, $x = a^2$.

results.title: The element y of Gardam's group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group $P$ with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2},\ a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$, $y = b^2$.

results.title: The element z of Gardam's group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group $P$ with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2},\ a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$, $z = (ab)^2$.

results.title: Group ring of Gardam's group over the field with two elements
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$ is the group ring of Gardam's group $P$ over the field $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Gardam's element p
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group ring $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$ of Gardam's group $P$ with generators $a$ and $b$, let $x = a^2$, $y = b^2$ and $z = (ab)^2$ in $P$, viewed as elements of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$. Then $p$ is the element $(1 + x)(1 + y)(1 + z^{-1})$ of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$.

results.title: Gardam's element q
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group ring $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$ of Gardam's group $P$ with generators $a$ and $b$, let $x = a^2$, $y = b^2$ and $z = (ab)^2$ in $P$, viewed as elements of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$. Then $q$ is the element $x^{-1}y^{-1} + x + y^{-1}z + z$ of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$.

results.title: Gardam's element r
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group ring $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$ of Gardam's group $P$ with generators $a$ and $b$, let $x = a^2$, $y = b^2$ and $z = (ab)^2$ in $P$, viewed as elements of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$. Then $r$ is the element $1 + x + y^{-1}z + xyz$ of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$.

results.title: Gardam's element s
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the group ring $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$ of Gardam's group $P$ with generators $a$ and $b$, let $x = a^2$, $y = b^2$ and $z = (ab)^2$ in $P$, viewed as elements of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$. Then $s$ is the element $1 + (x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1})z^{-1}$ of $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$.

results.title: Gardam's unit

results.title: Power-free natural numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. A natural number $n$ is $k$-free when $k \ge 2$, $n > 0$, and $p^k$ does not divide $n$ for any prime $p$.

results.title: Characterization of power-free numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $n$ is $k$-free if and only if $k \ge 2$, $n > 0$, and $p^k$ does not divide $n$ for any prime $p$.

results.title: The exponent of a power-free number is at least two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ is $k$-free, then $k \ge 2$.

results.title: Power-free numbers are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ is $k$-free, then $n > 0$.

results.title: A k-free number has no prime k-th power divisor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ is $k$-free and $p$ is a prime, then $p^k$ does not divide $n$.

results.title: Divisors of k-free numbers are k-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ is $k$-free and $m$ divides $n$, then $m$ is $k$-free.

results.title: Power-freeness is monotone in the exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ is $k$-free and $k \le l$, then $n$ is $l$-free.

results.title: A natural number is 2-free if and only if it is squarefree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, $n$ is $2$-free if and only if $n$ is squarefree, that is, $d^2$ divides $n$ only for $d = 1$.

results.title: Birational map
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ consists of dominant rational maps $f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y$ and $g \colon Y \dashrightarrow X$ that are mutually inverse: $g \circ f$ is the identity rational map of $X$ and $f \circ g$ is the identity rational map of $Y$.

results.title: Identity birational map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an irreducible scheme $X$, the identity birational map of $X$ has the identity rational map of $X$ as both its forward and its inverse map.

results.title: Inverse birational map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. The inverse of a birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is the birational map from $Y$ to $X$ whose forward map is the inverse rational map of the original and whose inverse map is its forward rational map.

results.title: Composition of birational maps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be irreducible schemes, let $f$ be a birational map from $X$ to $Y$ and let $g$ be a birational map from $Y$ to $Z$. The composite of $f$ and $g$ is the birational map from $X$ to $Z$ whose forward rational map is the forward map of $f$ followed by the forward map of $g$, and whose inverse rational map is the inverse of $g$ followed by the inverse of $f$.

results.title: Birational maps over a base
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes over a scheme $S$. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is over $S$ when its forward rational map $X \dashrightarrow Y$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.

results.title: Birational automorphisms over a base
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ be an irreducible scheme over a scheme $S$. The birational automorphisms of $X$ over $S$ form the subgroup of the group of birational self-maps of $X$ consisting of those birational maps whose forward rational map $X \dashrightarrow X$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.

results.title: Birational map of a partial isomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes and let $f$ be a partial isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$, that is, an isomorphism from a dense open subscheme of $X$ onto a dense open subscheme of $Y$. The birational map from $X$ to $Y$ given by $f$ has as forward map the rational map $X \dashrightarrow Y$ represented by $f$, and as inverse the rational map $Y \dashrightarrow X$ represented by the inverse of $f$.

results.title: Integral variety over a field
results.caption: Class
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field. A variety over $k$ in this sense is a scheme $X$ together with a morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ such that $X$ is integral (irreducible and reduced) and the morphism is separated and of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact).

results.title: Pseudo-isomorphism
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes. A partial isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$, that is, an isomorphism $U \cong V$ between dense open subschemes $U \subseteq X$ and $V \subseteq Y$, is a pseudo-isomorphism if it is an isomorphism in codimension one: every point of $X$ outside $U$ and every point of $Y$ outside $V$ has coheight at least $2$ in the specialization order of points.

results.title: Cremona group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a field $k$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$ is the group of birational automorphisms of affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$ over $\operatorname{Spec} k$.

results.title: Cremona group generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a field $k$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the proposition that the Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_n(k)$ is generated, as a group, by its pseudo-regularizable elements.

results.title: $\mathrm{Cr}_3$ of a number field is not generated by pseudo-regularizable elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a number field. The Cremona group $\mathrm{Cr}_3(k)$, the group of birational automorphisms of affine $3$-space over $k$, is not generated by its pseudo-regularizable elements.

results.title: Homothetic period pairs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A period pair is a pair $(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ of complex numbers that are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$, and its lattice is $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}\omega_1 + \mathbb{Z}\omega_2 \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Two period pairs $L$ and $L'$ with lattices $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$ are homothetic when there is a nonzero complex number $c$ such that $\Lambda' = c\Lambda = \{c\lambda : \lambda \in \Lambda\}$.

results.title: Homothety of period pairs is reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every period pair $L$ is homothetic to itself.

results.title: Homothety of period pairs is symmetric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a period pair $L$ is homothetic to a period pair $L'$, then $L'$ is homothetic to $L$.

results.title: Homothety of period pairs is transitive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For period pairs $L_1$, $L_2$, $L_3$, if $L_1$ is homothetic to $L_2$ and $L_2$ is homothetic to $L_3$, then $L_1$ is homothetic to $L_3$.

results.title: Homothety of period pairs is an equivalence relation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On period pairs, homothety is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

results.title: Volume of the cross-polytope
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the cross-polytope $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : |x_1| + \dots + |x_n| \le 1\}$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has volume $2^n / n!$.

results.title: Volume of the coordinate cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate cube $[-1, 1]^n$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has volume $2^n$.

results.title: Determinant formula for the area of a triangle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $x = (x_1, x_2)$ for the coordinates of a point $x$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. For all points $a, b, c$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the Lebesgue measure (area) of the convex hull of $\{a, b, c\}$, as a real number, equals $\frac{1}{2}\,\lvert (b_1 - a_1)(c_2 - a_2) - (b_2 - a_2)(c_1 - a_1) \rvert$.

results.title: Area of the unit square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The closed unit square $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : 0 \le x_1 \le 1 \text{ and } 0 \le x_2 \le 1\}$ in the Euclidean plane has Lebesgue measure (area) $1$.

results.title: Two-sided Hoeffding inequality for Bernoulli sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$ be independent real random variables on a probability space, each almost everywhere measurable, almost surely equal to $0$ or $1$, and with expectation $p$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Then the probability that $\lvert X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1} - np \rvert > \varepsilon n$ is at most $2 e^{-2 \varepsilon^2 n}$.

For natural numbers $g$ and $n$, a finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is a $g$-difference basis for $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ if $r_{A-A}(x) \ge g$ for every $x \in [n]$, and $\eta_g(n)$ is the least size of such a set.

results.title: Cyclic product numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, write $c(m, j)$ for the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. The cyclic product number $H(n, k)$ is the quotient $c(n + 1, k) / \binom{n + 1}{2}$, rounded down to a natural number, when $n + k$ is even (equivalently, $n - k$ is even), and $0$ when $n + k$ is odd. Division by zero gives $0$, so $H(0, k) = 0$ for every $k$.
